title: This is an exec() failure, not a shell's own message
explanation: `su - reportbot -c 'echo ok'` fails with `su: failed to execute /usr/local/sbin/corp-shell: No such file or directory` — that text comes from `su` itself reporting a failed `execve()`, not from anything reportbot's shell printed. su never got as far as running anything as reportbot at all.

title: Confirm the configured path is genuinely absent
explanation: `getent passwd reportbot` shows the account's shell field is `/usr/local/sbin/corp-shell`. `test -x /usr/local/sbin/corp-shell` (or `ls -l` it) confirms there's simply nothing at that path — not a permissions problem, not a broken symlink, just an entry that was never actually deployed alongside the account.

title: A missing binary is a different failure mode than an intentional lockout
explanation: A `nologin`-shell account fails because a real, installed binary runs and deliberately refuses — a working policy decision. This account fails because `execve()` can't find anything to run at all before any policy, lockout or otherwise, ever gets a chance to execute. The two produce superficially similar 'can't get a shell' symptoms but point at completely different root causes and completely different fixes.

title: Without a fixture to reinstall, point the account at a shell that exists
explanation: There's no package or copy of the custom wrapper available inside this box to restore the original setup. The pragmatic fix under time pressure is `sudo usermod -s /bin/bash reportbot` — get automation running again on a real shell, and treat the wrapper's disappearance as a separate follow-up rather than something blocking the immediate incident.

title: Verify with the same command that originally failed
explanation: `su - reportbot -c 'echo ok'` succeeding confirms `execve()` now has something real to run — the specific failure class from step 1 is gone, distinct from just checking that `getent passwd` shows a different path.
